**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/01/24 (Tue) 03:54
- [USER] CHAPTER SEVEN RULE #2 Be Still So You Can Heal (The Neutral Spine) From Jeremy
- [USER] Let’s assume that you are beginning to get the big picture. 
- [USER] You have also begun to identify the “dumb” things that you’ve been doing to wreck your back, and that you have stopped doing them.
- [USER] It is time to start the healing, and that is a matter of immobilizing your lower back or lumbar spine so it can heal.
- [USER] Think of your tortured back as being like a broken arm or leg.
- [USER] When you break an arm, the doc puts it in a stiff cast so you can’t bang it or twist it and to give it time and rest to heal.
- [USER] We can’t do anything quite as dramatic as put you in a whole-body cast for your damaged back.
- [USER] We can show you how to carry yourself so that you effectively immobilize your lower back.
- [USER] If you do not immobilize your back, it will not heal—simple as that.
- [USER] Maintaining a neutral spine is at the heart of your cure, and will be at the heart of your life after your cure.
- [USER] This is the time to learn how to achieve a neutral spine and how to maintain it all the time.
- [USER] The spine is a meticulously engineered piece of machinery, but it has a lot of redundancy built in.
- [USER] Take the pressure of bad posture—and dumb movement patterns—off, and there is very likely enough “room” in this spine for the sufferer to have a normal life.
- [USER] “Neutral” means the position in which the least amount of problem loads occur, all up and down the spine.
- [USER] If you keep your spine in neutral, those inflamed joints and nerve roots will likely calm down if you leave them alone for a while.
- [USER] Learning to keep a neutral spine is not totally easy.
- [USER] This is the “cast” that lets your body heal.
- [USER] Step one is understanding the concept of neutral spine.
- [USER] Step two is learning to find it and lock it in place, and keep it in place forever.
- [USER] The neutral spine is the position that allows your spine to do its job with the least amount of stress and load.
- [USER] If you have already damaged your back, it is the position that results in the least amount of new damage or pain.
- [USER] For most people, the picture on the left is the neutral spine.
- [USER] Note the gentle curve of the lower back in the “good” spine.
